comments.text:
Scalpers do not take computer parts out of the market, and they do not hodl inventory. All scalping does is redistribute products from people who have time to people who have money.

Computer part scalping is not at all like event ticket scalping. Event tickets are weird economically, because the total quantity is fixed and their value peaks and then goes to zero near-instantly over the first few minutes of the event, and everybody knows it. With tickets, the scalpers' advatage is that he bought tickets early, and all the scalpers are in a game of chicken with one another. 

With computer parts, the scalper's advantage is that he has knowledge of something being sold below current market value, and the time/ability to execute the trade (which might require standing in line at 5 am or idling in a bunch of Discord servers).  The computer part scalper has found a trade route, and he wants to run it as many times as he can before it dries up.
